purpose: Check whether a SocratiCode instance (and a freshly spawned one) reconnects to its Qdrant backend after Qdrant is killed and restarted on the same port/data dir, without any client-side reconfiguration, and whether the index state survives.
preregistered: If both the already-running SocratiCode process and a newly spawned one continue to report the full, correct indexed-chunk count and answer queries after the Qdrant restart with zero config changes, SocratiCode-side reconnection is established for this disposable pair (supports_incumbent, scoped to same-host process restart, not full-service/native-client MCP reconnection which this unit does not test per the binding rules).

commands.cmd: python3 <scratch>/rag-ops/gap9_qdrant_restart.py  # 402-file project already fully indexed (402 chunks) from the gap-1 run; record status/search/point-counts; pgrep+SIGKILL9 the disposable qdrant process (pid 2046732, port 26333, NOT the live qdrant-agent-lab.service on pid 402); relaunch qdrant with the identical --config-path (same data dir, same port); wait for /collections to answer; re-query the SAME already-open SocratiCode MCP process, then spawn a brand-new SocratiCode process with identical env and query it too
commands.output_excerpt: qdrant_reachable_immediately_after_kill=False; qdrant back up after 1s; same-process status after restart: 'Indexed chunks: 402' (unchanged); fresh-process status after restart: 'Indexed chunks: 402' (unchanged); search for 'modulo watcher marker' returned real matches post-restart; qdrant point counts identical before/after (codebase_2df0d90218d3=402, symgraph collections unchanged, socraticode_metadata=2)

commands.cmd: ps aux | grep qdrant  # confirm the live agent-lab qdrant (pid 402, qdrant-agent-lab.yaml) was never touched
commands.output_excerpt: seath 402 ... qdrant --config-path .../qdrant-agent-lab.yaml --disable-telemetry (untouched, same pid throughout); seath 2047251 ... qdrant-disposable.yaml (the new disposable pid after restart)

result: On the disposable stack, killing the Qdrant process (SIGKILL) and restarting it with the identical config (same http_port=26333, same on-disk storage_path) restores full service within 1 second. Both an already-connected SocratiCode process and a brand-new one (same QDRANT_URL env var, no config change) correctly report the pre-restart index state (402/402 chunks) and successfully answer a semantic search query afterward. Qdrant point counts were bit-for-bit identical before and after (on-disk persistence, not an in-memory cache), so no data loss was observed for this same-host restart. The live agent-lab Qdrant instance (separate pid, separate config file, separate port) was confirmed running unaffected throughout via ps aux.

verdict_impact.explanation: This closes the specific sub-claim the gap named as missing: SocratiCode-side reconnection to a restarted Qdrant, both for an already-open client and a fresh one, with zero manual reconfiguration. It does NOT establish 'SocratiCode full-service restart' (we restarted only Qdrant, not the SocratiCode process itself simultaneously) or 'native-client rebinding' (we did not restart/reconnect an actual Claude/Codex MCP client session, per the binding rule that live MCP client sessions of running Claude sessions are off limits). Those two remaining sub-claims stay open and are recorded as not tested here, so the gap is only partially settled.

limitations: Only Qdrant was restarted; SocratiCode's own process (and the live vLLM embedding server) were left running throughout, so this does not test 'SocratiCode full-service restart' as the gap's next_check literally asks.

Native Claude/Codex MCP client reconnection was not tested (explicitly out of scope per the binding rules, which forbid touching the Context Mode processes of running Claude sessions); recorded here as not tested, not as passing.
Single restart cycle, single host, no concurrent writers during the outage window -- does not test reconnection under write contention.
Qdrant was down for only ~1s in this test; a longer outage or a crash that corrupts the on-disk segment files was not exercised.
